title: Are LLM-based Evaluators Confusing NLG Quality Criteria?

bias_targets.methodology: Using 18 fine-grained, aspect-targeted perturbation attacks (e.g., introducing grammatical errors, contradictions, or passive voice) to measure whether LLM-based evaluators inappropriately conflate independent text quality criteria (such as penalizing coherence or simplicity when only grammatical errors are present).

Applying repetition-based perturbations to source texts to observe if LLMs fail to penalize redundant information during fluency evaluation, thereby revealing an inherent tolerance or preference for longer, repetitive outputs.
